quests.instruction: Match each word to the meaning that fits.

pairs.value: Needing rest because your energy is low.
Feeling pleased about something good.
Feeling unhappy, often after bad news.

quests.hint: Two of these feelings come from good or bad news. The third comes from something else entirely.
quests.explanation: Happy and sad sit on opposite ends of the same scale, one for good news and one for bad. Tired is a different kind of feeling — it comes from your body needing rest, not from anything that happened.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The main meal, usually eaten in the evening.
The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.
The meal eaten in the middle of the day.

quests.hint: Think about your own day: which meal comes first, which comes next, and which comes last?
quests.explanation: These three words follow the order of a normal day. Breakfast opens it, lunch sits in the middle, and dinner closes it.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A girl or woman with the same parents as you.
A man who has a child.
A woman who has a child.

quests.hint: Two of these words describe your parents. The third describes someone your own age.
quests.explanation: Mother and father are the two people who raise a child. Sister is different — she's from the same generation as you, not the one before it.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A piece of furniture you sit on.
Pages joined together with words for reading.
A tool used for writing with ink.

quests.hint: Picture a study desk: one of these you read, one you write with, one you sit on.
quests.explanation: A book is made for reading and a pen is made for writing, so both involve words in some way. A chair has nothing to do with words at all — its only job is to hold you up while you sit.
quests.paragraphTopic: Things you find at a desk

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: To push yourself off the ground into the air.
To move quickly using your legs.
To move at a normal, unhurried speed on foot.

quests.hint: Two of these keep your feet on the ground. One doesn't.
quests.explanation: Walking and running both move you forward on foot, just at different speeds. Jumping is a completely different motion — for a moment, your feet leave the ground.

quests.instruction: Match each word with what it means.

pairs.value: A person who operates a vehicle.
A person trained to treat sick people.
A person whose job is to help others learn.

quests.hint: Each word names a job. Ask yourself what that person actually spends their day doing.
quests.explanation: A doctor treats illness and a teacher helps students learn — both jobs focus on people directly. A driver's job is different: it centers on getting somewhere safely, not on treating or teaching anyone.
quests.paragraphTopic: Common jobs and what they involve

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Clothing you wear on your head.
Items you wear to cover and protect your feet.
Clothing you wear on the top part of your body.

quests.hint: Work from head to toe: which item goes where?
quests.explanation: A hat sits at the top of you and shoes sit at the bottom, so between them they cover the two ends of your body. A shirt fills in the middle, covering your chest and back.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Having a pleasant, gentle heat — not hot and not cold.
Having a very high temperature.
Having a very low temperature.

quests.hint: Where would a cup of tea sit between ice and fire?
quests.explanation: Hot and cold mark the two far ends of temperature. Warm sits in the middle — it's the word people usually reach for when something feels comfortable, like a warm jacket.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A two-wheeled vehicle you ride by pedaling.
A large vehicle that carries many passengers on roads.
A vehicle that travels on tracks, often carrying many people.

quests.hint: Two of these carry a crowd. One is usually ridden alone.
quests.explanation: A bus and a train both move large groups of people, though a bus stays on the road while a train needs tracks. A bicycle carries just one rider, powered by their own legs instead of an engine.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The room used for washing and using the toilet.
The room where meals are cooked.
The room where a person sleeps.

quests.hint: Walk through a home in your mind and name what happens in each room.
quests.explanation: A kitchen is built around cooking and a bedroom around sleeping — two very different daily routines. A bathroom covers a third routine again, washing, separate from either of the others.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: To fasten something with a key so it cannot be opened.
To move something so it is no longer shut.
To shut something that was open.

quests.hint: All three could describe what you do to a door before leaving the house, but one goes further than the others.
quests.explanation: Open and close are opposite actions on a door — letting it swing one way or the other. Lock goes a step beyond close: it makes sure the door stays shut until someone uses a key.
quests.paragraphTopic: Actions you do to a door

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The day after today.
The day before today.
The day that is happening right now.

quests.hint: One of these has already passed, one is happening now, and one hasn't arrived yet.
quests.explanation: Today marks the present moment. Yesterday points backward to the day before it, while tomorrow points forward to the day after — together the three words cover past, present, and future.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A white drink that comes from cows or other animals.
A round fruit that grows on trees.
A food made from baked flour and water.

quests.hint: A trip to the grocery store would put all three of these in your basket.
quests.explanation: An apple grows on a tree and is eaten whole, while bread is baked from flour and usually sliced. Milk is different from both — it's a drink, not something you chew.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: To give money for something you receive.
To get something by giving money for it.
To give something to someone in exchange for money.

quests.hint: Money moves in every one of these actions, just not in the same direction each time.
quests.explanation: Buying and selling are two sides of the same exchange — one person buys while another sells. Paying is really the part in the middle: the actual moment the money changes hands.

quests.instruction: Match each word with what it means.

pairs.value: Having a great length from one end to the other.
Large in size.
Little in size.

quests.hint: Two of these describe overall size. One measures just a single direction.
quests.explanation: Big and small are opposites that describe how much space something takes up altogether. Long measures something narrower — just the distance from one end to the other, not the whole object.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: An animal with feathers and wings that can usually fly.
A common pet animal known for barking and loyalty.
A small pet animal known for purring and independence.

quests.hint: Two of these animals usually live indoors as pets. One is more often seen outside, or in a cage.
quests.explanation: Dogs and cats are both popular house pets, though they behave very differently — one barks, the other purrs. A bird stands apart from both because of its feathers and its ability to fly.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: To pay attention to sounds, especially someone speaking.
To look at words and understand their meaning.
To make letters or words on paper or a screen.

quests.hint: Two of these skills involve words on a page. The third uses your ears instead.
quests.explanation: Reading and writing both deal with words on a page — one for taking them in, the other for putting them down. Listening works differently, since it depends on your ears rather than your eyes.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Air that moves, sometimes strongly.
Water that falls from clouds in drops.
Soft white ice that falls from the sky in cold weather.

quests.hint: Look up at the sky: two of these fall down, one simply moves past.
quests.explanation: Rain and snow both fall from above, though rain is liquid and snow is frozen. Wind isn't something that falls at all — it's air moving, often felt rather than seen.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: To let tears fall, often from sadness or pain.
To curve your mouth upward to show happiness.
To make sounds of happiness, often at something funny.

quests.hint: Your face changes in its own way for each of these.
quests.explanation: Smiling and laughing both show happiness, though laughing is louder and usually comes from something funny. Crying sits at the opposite end of the scale — it's usually a sign of sadness or pain, not joy.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A shop where you collect or buy medicine.
A large building where seriously ill or injured people are treated.
A small clinic where you visit a doctor for check-ups.

quests.hint: If you felt unwell, you might visit any of these three places, but for different reasons.
quests.explanation: A doctor's office usually handles quick, routine visits, while a hospital treats more serious problems and can keep patients overnight. A pharmacy is different from both — it's where you go afterward to collect your medicine.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Moving your body to the rhythm of music.
A sport played by kicking a ball into a goal.
Moving through water using your arms and legs.

quests.hint: One of these needs a ball, one needs water, and one needs music.
quests.explanation: Soccer is a team sport built around a ball, while swimming happens in water and needs no ball at all. Dancing is different again — it's about moving with music, not scoring points or racing.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A screen used mainly for watching shows and movies.
A device used to call or message other people.
An electronic device used for work, browsing, or storing information.

quests.hint: You might own all three of these, but each one does its own job.
quests.explanation: A phone is mainly for talking or messaging someone, and a computer is built for tasks like writing or browsing online. A television is different from both — it's made for watching, not typing or calling.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: In a short amount of time from now.
Before the expected or usual time.
After the expected or usual time.

quests.hint: Two of these compare to a time you expected. The third doesn't need one.
quests.explanation: Early and late are opposites, each measured against a time you expected something to happen. Soon works differently — it doesn't compare to any expected time; it just means something is close.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The covering on top of a building.
An opening in a wall, usually with glass, that lets in light.
An opening used to enter or leave a building.

quests.hint: Walk around the outside of a house: what lets light in, what do you walk through, and what sits on top?
quests.explanation: A window lets light in and lets you see outside, while a door is what you actually walk through. A roof isn't part of that pair at all — it covers the whole building from above.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Someone you do not know at all.
Someone you know well and like spending time with.
Someone who lives near you.

quests.hint: How close is each person to you: very close, a little close, or not at all?
quests.explanation: A friend is someone you know and like, while a neighbor is simply someone who lives nearby — you might not know them well. A stranger sits at the far end of that scale, someone you've never met.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: The part of the day after the sun goes down.
The early part of the day, after sunrise.
The part of the day between noon and evening.

quests.hint: The day splits into three parts here. Which comes first?
quests.explanation: Morning opens the day just after sunrise, and afternoon carries it forward once noon has passed. Night comes last, once the sun has set completely.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Costing no money at all.
Costing very little money.
Costing a lot of money.

quests.hint: Line these up from paying nothing to paying a lot.
quests.explanation: Cheap and expensive sit at opposite ends of price, one low and one high. Free goes further than cheap — it means there's no cost at all.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A place where travelers pay to sleep for a night or more.
A place where planes take off and land.
A place where trains or buses stop for passengers.

quests.hint: You'd pass through two of these quickly, then settle in at the third overnight.
quests.explanation: An airport serves planes and a station serves trains or buses — both are places you pass through while traveling. A hotel breaks that pattern, since it's where you stay once you've arrived, not somewhere you just pass through.

quests.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.value: To keep doing something without stopping.
To start doing something.
To complete something and stop doing it.

quests.hint: One of these starts an activity, one ends it, and one keeps it going.
quests.explanation: Begin marks the start of something and finish marks its end. Continue sits between the two — it means the activity keeps going instead of stopping at either end.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Making no noise at all.
Making a lot of noise.
Making very little noise.

quests.hint: Rank these from a lot of noise down to none at all.
quests.explanation: Loud and quiet are opposites, describing a lot of noise versus very little. Silent goes even further than quiet — it means there's no sound at all.
